components.note: 宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 安, 室; 完 first meant complete, whole.
元 (yuán) is a close sound clue for wán; 元 also sounds out 玩 wán, 院 yuàn and 远 yuǎn.
彐 (hand-like part) — 事 is usually explained as a hand holding a tool or tally, 'handling business' — a hedged reading, not certain.
史 (history, scribe) — shares an ancient root with 事: a hand holding a recording tool. Both are about handling official 'matters'.

example.hanzi: 这件事很快就能完事。
example.pinyin: zhè jiàn shì hěn kuài jiù néng wánshì.
example.english: This matter can be finished very quickly.
example.fact: Barcelona's Sagrada Família basilica has been under continuous construction since 1882, funded largely by private donations and ticket sales rather than government money, with completion now projected around 2026 — well over 140 years after ground was first broken. Architect Antoni Gaudí knew he would never see it finished in his lifetime and reportedly said that was fine, since 'my client is not in a hurry.'

examples.hanzi: 你先吃饭，我完事了就来。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ xiān chīfàn, wǒ wánshì le jiù lái.
examples.english: You eat first, and I'll come once I'm done.

examples.hanzi: 等他完事以后，我们再走。
examples.pinyin: Děng tā wánshì yǐhòu, wǒmen zài zǒu.
examples.english: Once he is finished, we'll leave.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand radical — 播 is scattering seed by hand, then broadcasting.
番 (fān) — near sound — 播 is bō; 番 also sounds out 翻 fān and 潘 pān.
凵 (open pit) — oldest form shows a foot stepping out of a pit or cave: to go out, come out.

example.hanzi: 这部电视剧将在周五晚上播出。
example.pinyin: zhè bù diànshìjù jiāng zài zhōuwǔ wǎnshàng bōchū.
example.english: This TV drama will be broadcast on Friday evening.
example.fact: Pittsburgh radio station KDKA's broadcast of the 1920 U.S. presidential election results is widely cited as the first regularly scheduled commercial radio broadcast in American history. The station had only just received its official license days earlier, and its early success helped spark a nationwide radio boom within just a few years.

examples.hanzi: 这场比赛将在电视上播出。
examples.pinyin: Zhè chǎng bǐsài jiāng zài diànshì shàng bōchū.
examples.english: This match will be broadcast on TV.

examples.hanzi: 这个节目每天晚上七点播出。
examples.pinyin: Zhège jiémù měi tiān wǎnshang qī diǎn bōchū.
examples.english: This program airs at seven every evening.

meanings: one's own (child) (i.e. one's child by birth)

components.note: 亲 (qīn) keeps the sound part of the traditional 親, which also had 见; it also gives 新 xīn and 薪 xīn, so qīn/xīn is a series.
土 (earth) — a green shoot pushing up from the ground: growth, birth, life. 生 also sounds out 性 xìng, 姓 xìng and 星 xīng.

example.hanzi: 她终于找到了自己的亲生父母。
example.pinyin: tā zhōngyú zhǎodàole zìjǐ de qīnshēng fùmǔ.
example.english: She finally found her biological parents.
example.fact: Identical twins share nearly all of their DNA, yet they still have different fingerprints, because fingerprint ridges are shaped not just by genes but by random pressures and fluid movements inside the womb during early development. This is why fingerprints remain one of the most reliable ways to distinguish between even genetically identical individuals.

examples.hanzi: 她是我的亲生妹妹。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì wǒ de qīnshēng mèimei.
examples.english: She is my biological younger sister.

examples.hanzi: 他对养子像对亲生儿子一样好。
examples.pinyin: Tā duì yǎngzǐ xiàng duì qīnshēng érzi yíyàng hǎo.
examples.english: He treats his adopted son as well as his own child.

components.note: 辶 (walk, 走之旁) — movement and roads: 过, 进, 送; 运 is to move, then to be moved by luck.
云 (yún) is a near sound match for yùn.
用 (use) — early picture is debated: a pail, a fenced enclosure or a hung bell. Memory aid: a door-frame 冂 with a cross-bar — a tool 'put to use' (使用, 不用).

example.hanzi: 他善于运用所学的知识解决问题。
example.pinyin: tā shànyú yùnyòng suǒxué de zhīshì jiějué wèntí.
example.english: He is skilled at applying what he has learned to solve problems.
example.fact: The application of Bernoulli's principle, which describes how a fluid's pressure drops as its speed increases, underlies how an airplane's curved wing generates the lift needed to fly. Daniel Bernoulli formulated the mathematical basis for this relationship in 1738, more than a century and a half before the Wright brothers' first flight.

examples.hanzi: 学生们要学会运用所学的知识。
examples.pinyin: Xuéshengmen yào xuéhuì yùnyòng suǒ xué de zhīshi.
examples.english: Students should learn to apply what they have learned.

examples.hanzi: 这篇文章运用了很多生动的比喻。
examples.pinyin: Zhè piān wénzhāng yùnyòng le hěn duō shēngdòng de bǐyù.
examples.english: This article uses many vivid metaphors.

components.note: 大 (big person) — a person with a line above the head, marking the sky above; tiān = heaven, sky, day.
真 (zhēn) is a sound clue for 镇 zhèn and 慎 shèn; 真 means real, true.

example.hanzi: 孩子的天真笑容让人感到温暖。
example.pinyin: háizi de tiānzhēn xiàoróng ràng rén gǎndào wēnnuǎn.
example.english: The child's innocent smile makes people feel warm.
example.fact: On the Galápagos Islands, many native animals evolved for millennia with no natural land predators, which is why finches and iguanas there famously showed little fear when Charles Darwin and other early visitors first arrived. That naive lack of caution, largely absent in animals from predator-rich mainland habitats, was one of the features that first caught Darwin's attention.

examples.hanzi: 你太天真了，世界没那么简单。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ tài tiānzhēn le, shìjiè méi nàme jiǎndān.
examples.english: You're too naive, the world isn't that simple.

examples.hanzi: 小女孩天真地问：“月亮会跟着我走吗？”
examples.pinyin: Xiǎo nǚhái tiānzhēn de wèn: “Yuèliang huì gēnzhe wǒ zǒu ma?”
examples.english: The little girl asked innocently, “Does the moon follow me?”

components.note: 亻 (person) — a servant is a person; also in 他 he, 们 plural.
卜 (bǔ) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 扑 pū and 朴 pǔ.
人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.

example.hanzi: 这位贵族雇了好几个仆人。
example.pinyin: zhè wèi guìzú gùle hǎo jǐ gè púrén.
example.english: This nobleman employed several servants.
example.fact: In Victorian-era Britain, a single large aristocratic household could employ dozens of servants, from butlers and footmen to scullery maids, each with strictly defined duties and a place in a rigid internal hierarchy. Historians estimate that by the late 1800s, domestic service was the single largest employment category for working-class women in England.

examples.hanzi: 仆人把茶端到了客厅。
examples.pinyin: Púrén bǎ chá duān dào le kètīng.
examples.english: The servant brought the tea to the living room.

examples.hanzi: 这个故事里的仆人很聪明。
examples.pinyin: Zhège gùshi lǐ de púrén hěn cōngmíng.
examples.english: The servant in this story is very clever.

components.note: 氵 (water) — slippery as wet surfaces; also in 河 river, 海 sea.
骨 (gǔ) is only a loose sound clue; 猾 huá shares it and sounds exactly like 滑.
禾 (grain) — crops and harvest, as in 种 plant, 秋 autumn, 稻 rice.
旨 (zhǐ) is only a loose sound clue for jī.

example.hanzi: 他的动作十分滑稽,把大家都逗笑了。
example.pinyin: tā de dòngzuò shífēn huájī, bǎ dàjiā dōu dòuxiàole.
example.english: His movements were very comical and made everyone laugh.
example.fact: Laughter triggers the release of endorphins in the brain and can measurably lower levels of stress hormones in the body, effects studied by researchers in a field sometimes called gelotology. Some hospitals have used this research to justify formal 'laughter therapy' programs aimed at reducing pain and anxiety in patients.

examples.hanzi: 这个小丑的表演太滑稽了。
examples.pinyin: Zhège xiǎochǒu de biǎoyǎn tài huájī le.
examples.english: This clown's performance is so funny.

examples.hanzi: 他戴着一顶滑稽的帽子。
examples.pinyin: Tā dàizhe yì dǐng huájī de màozi.
examples.english: He is wearing a comical hat.

components.note: 心 (heart) — feelings and thought, as in 想 think, 思 ponder, 急 anxious; in 怎 it is only loosely linked to the question sense.
乍 (zhà) is a loose sound clue for zěn; 乍 also sounds out 作 zuò, 昨 zuó and 炸 zhà.
幺 (tiny, a thread) — 么 looks like 幺 and was borrowed as a simplified form for the light particle in 什么, 怎么, 这么. The shape does not explain the meaning today.
厶 (loop) — the visible lower part, a small curl. Memory aid: a tiny stroke 丿 over a curl — a 'little something' you ask about: 什么 what?
著 (zhù / zhe) — older form of 着: 艹 plant + 者 (zhě) as sound. 着 is a variant with 羊 over 目; neither part gives the 'in progress' sense.
目 (eye) — the bottom. The eye family: 看, 眼, 睛, 睡. In 着 it is only part of a variant shape. Memory aid: 睡着 — eyes 目 shut, asleep.

example.hanzi: 这事儿你打算怎么着?
example.pinyin: zhè shìr nǐ dǎsuàn zěnmezhāo?
example.english: What are you going to do about this matter?
example.fact: A widely cited study from the University of Michigan found that young children ask several hundred questions a day on average during their peak years of curiosity, far more than most adults realize. Researchers see this relentless questioning as a key driver of early cognitive development, helping children build working models of how the world operates.

examples.hanzi: 你要是不同意，那怎么着？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ yàoshi bù tóngyì, nà zěnmezhāo?
examples.english: If you don't agree, then what?

examples.hanzi: 怎么着，你还想再来一次吗？
examples.pinyin: Zěnmezhāo, nǐ hái xiǎng zài lái yí cì ma?
examples.english: So what, do you want to go another round?

components.note: 日 (sun) — marks light and warmth, as in 晴, 暗, 暖; 暖 is sunny warmth.
爰 (yuán) is a loose hint for nuǎn; 缓 huǎn and 援 yuán share it.

example.hanzi: 今天天气真暖和。
example.pinyin: Jīntiān tiānqì zhēn nuǎnhuo.
example.english: The weather is really warm today.
example.fact: 暖和 (nuǎnhuo) is the colloquial adjective for pleasantly warm. 暖气 is central heating in northern China, 温暖 is warm in an emotional sense, and 暖男 describes a considerate, caring man.

examples.hanzi: 冬天屋里有暖气，很暖和。
examples.pinyin: Dōngtiān wū lǐ yǒu nuǎnqì, hěn nuǎnhuo.
examples.english: In winter the room has heating and is very warm.

examples.hanzi: 喝杯热茶暖一暖身子吧。
examples.pinyin: Hē bēi rè chá nuǎn yi nuǎn shēnzi ba.
examples.english: Have a cup of hot tea to warm yourself up.

components.note: 壴 (drum) — a picture of a drum on a stand; 鼓 adds a hand with a stick 支 beating it.

example.hanzi: 他在乐队里打鼓。
example.pinyin: Tā zài yuèduì lǐ dǎ gǔ.
example.english: He plays the drums in the band.
example.fact: 鼓 is a drum, and the verb extends to "stir up" or "bulge": 鼓掌 (to applaud), 鼓励 (to encourage), 鼓起勇气 (to summon courage). The measure word for a drum is 面 or 通 (for a round of beating).

examples.hanzi: 小朋友们在敲鼓。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎopéngyǒumen zài qiāo gǔ.
examples.english: The kids are beating the drum.

examples.hanzi: 大家鼓掌欢迎新同学。
examples.pinyin: Dàjiā gǔzhǎng huānyíng xīn tóngxué.
examples.english: Everyone applauded to welcome the new classmate.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 氵 is water, as in 海, 河, 湖; 漫 is water overflowing, then spreading freely.
曼 (màn) — same sound — 漫 is màn; 曼 also sounds out 慢 màn.
长 (long, grow) — simplified from 長, an old person with long hair. Read cháng "long" or zhǎng "to grow, elder".

example.hanzi: 这是一段漫长而艰难的旅程。
example.pinyin: zhè shì yī duàn màncháng ér jiānnán de lǚchéng.
example.english: This was a long and difficult journey.
example.fact: Light from the Andromeda Galaxy, the nearest large galaxy to our own, takes about 2.5 million years to reach Earth, meaning the light arriving tonight left long before modern humans existed. Despite that immense distance, Andromeda is on a slow collision course with the Milky Way, with the two galaxies expected to merge in roughly four billion years.

examples.hanzi: 冬天的夜晚特别漫长。
examples.pinyin: Dōngtiān de yèwǎn tèbié màncháng.
examples.english: Winter nights are especially long.

examples.hanzi: 我们经过了漫长的等待。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen jīngguò le màncháng de děngdài.
examples.english: We went through a long wait.

meanings: (Buddhism) to free oneself of worldly worries

components.note: 角 (horn) — an ox's horn; with 刀 (knife) the picture is cutting up an ox, so "to take apart", then to loosen and explain.
刀 (knife) — cutting, as in 分, 切, 到; a blade separates the parts.
月 (flesh) — ⺼ is the body radical (月 in 脸, 脑); 脱 is slipping off a layer, like skin or clothes.
兑 (duì) — near sound — 脱 is tuō; 兑 also sounds out 说 shuō and 税 shuì.

example.hanzi: 冥想帮助他从压力中解脱出来。
example.pinyin: míngxiǎng bāngzhù tā cóng yālì zhōng jiětuō chūlái.
example.english: Meditation helped him free himself from stress.
example.fact: The practice of mindfulness meditation traces back over 2,500 years to early Buddhist traditions in India, but modern neuroscience has confirmed real physical effects: MRI studies show that eight weeks of regular meditation can measurably shrink the amygdala, the brain region that drives the stress response.

examples.hanzi: 考试结束后，我终于感到解脱了。
examples.pinyin: Kǎoshì jiéshù hòu, wǒ zhōngyú gǎndào jiětuō le.
examples.english: After the exam ended, I finally felt relieved.

examples.hanzi: 他想从繁重的工作中解脱出来。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiǎng cóng fánzhòng de gōngzuò zhōng jiětuō chūlái.
examples.english: He wants to get free from his heavy workload.

components.note: 忄 (heart) — a timid heart; also in 怕 afraid, 快 happy.
需 (xū) is a loose clue; 儒 rú shares it.
大 (person) — a man with a hairpin 一 on his head, a grown man; 夫 also gives 扶 fú and 肤 fū.

example.hanzi: 面对危险时逃跑的人常被称为懦夫。
example.pinyin: miànduì wēixiǎn shí táopǎo de rén cháng bèi chēngwéi nuòfū.
example.english: Someone who runs away in the face of danger is often called a coward.
example.fact: The 'fight-or-flight' response was first named in 1915 by physiologist Walter Cannon, who found that a surge of adrenaline prepares an animal's body to confront a threat or flee it within seconds. Freezing in place, sometimes mistaken for cowardice, is actually a third survival strategy — many prey animals, from rabbits to deer, freeze first because sudden stillness can make a predator lose track of them.

examples.hanzi: 别当懦夫，勇敢地说出来吧。
examples.pinyin: Bié dāng nuòfū, yǒnggǎn de shuō chūlái ba.
examples.english: Don't be a coward, speak up bravely.

examples.hanzi: 他觉得不敢道歉的人是懦夫。
examples.pinyin: Tā juéde bù gǎn dàoqiàn de rén shì nuòfū.
examples.english: He thinks people who dare not apologize are cowards.

components.note: 贝 (cowry shell, money) — 责 first meant demanding payment of a debt, hence duty. 责 sounds out 债 zhài, 积 jī and 绩 jì.
忄 (heart) — feelings, as in 快, 忙, 情: a strange feeling.
圣 here is not the "sage" word; it is only a loose sound clue for guài.

example.hanzi: 他为迟到的事责怪自己的车。
example.pinyin: tā wèi chídào de shì zéguài zìjǐ de chē.
example.english: He blamed his car for being late.
example.fact: In 1977, psychologist Lee Ross coined the term 'fundamental attribution error' to describe humans' tendency to blame other people's failures on their character while excusing our own identical mistakes as caused by circumstance — a bias later replicated across many different cultures.

examples.hanzi: 这件事不能责怪孩子。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì bù néng zéguài háizi.
examples.english: You can't blame the child for this.

examples.hanzi: 他们互相责怪，谁也不肯认错。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen hùxiāng zéguài, shéi yě bù kěn rèncuò.
examples.english: They blamed each other and neither would admit fault.

components.note: 纟 (thread, simplified 糸) — silk and cord words: 红 red, 给 give, 线 line; a thread has an end, which fits 终 end.
冬 (dōng) rhymes with 终 zhōng, and 冬 originally meant the end (of the year) too — so it helps sound and sense.
纟 (silk thread, simplified 糸) — threads and ties, as in 红, 给, 经; 结 is a knot.
吉 (jí) is a close sound clue for jié; 吉 also sounds out 洁 jié.

example.hanzi: 这场战争终于迎来了终结。
example.pinyin: zhè chǎng zhànzhēng zhōngyú yíngláile zhōngjié.
example.english: This war finally came to an end.
example.fact: The Hundred Years' War, despite its name, actually spanned 116 years (1337-1453) and only ended when French forces retook Bordeaux, the last English stronghold on the European continent.

examples.hanzi: 这个故事有一个圆满的终结。
examples.pinyin: Zhège gùshi yǒu yí ge yuánmǎn de zhōngjié.
examples.english: This story has a happy ending.

examples.hanzi: 一场大雪终结了这个漫长的秋天。
examples.pinyin: Yì chǎng dàxuě zhōngjié le zhège màncháng de qiūtiān.
examples.english: A heavy snowfall brought this long autumn to an end.

components.note: 廾 (two hands) — two hands joined — 共 is doing together; it also sounds out 供 gōng.
彐 (hand-like part) — 事 is usually explained as a hand holding a tool or tally, 'handling business' — a hedged reading, not certain.
史 (history, scribe) — shares an ancient root with 事: a hand holding a recording tool. Both are about handling official 'matters'.

example.hanzi: 我和他共事了十年。
example.pinyin: wǒ hé tā gòngshìle shí nián.
example.english: I have worked together with him for ten years.
example.fact: Leafcutter ant colonies divide labor so precisely that some workers specialize purely as living trash compactors, packing waste into underground chambers, while others cultivate the fungus gardens the colony depends on for food — a division of labor among genetically identical sisters that biologists have studied for over a century.

examples.hanzi: 我们俩在同一个项目里共事。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen liǎ zài tóng yí ge xiàngmù lǐ gòngshì.
examples.english: The two of us work together on the same project.

examples.hanzi: 他是个很容易共事的人。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì ge hěn róngyì gòngshì de rén.
examples.english: He is someone who is easy to work with.

components.note: 西 (west) — traditionally a bird settling on its nest at sunset, hence west; 西 turns up in 要 and 栖.
隹 (short-tailed bird) — marks birds, as in 难, 谁 (loan uses), 集; 雅 first named a crow, now borrowed for 'elegant'.
牙 (yá) hints at the sound: 雅 yǎ is close to 鸦 yā and 呀 ya.
囗 (enclosure) — boundaries and surroundings: 国 country, 园 garden, 回 return; 图 is a drawn plan of a region.

example.hanzi: 西雅图以经常下雨著称。
example.pinyin: xīyǎtú yǐ jīngcháng xiàyǔ zhùchēng.
example.english: Seattle is known for its frequent rain.
example.fact: Despite its reputation for rain, Seattle actually receives less annual precipitation than New York City, Miami, or Houston — its fame for grey weather instead comes from the sheer number of overcast days, over 200 a year, caused by the Pacific jet stream pushing low clouds against the Cascade and Olympic mountains.

examples.hanzi: 我哥哥在西雅图的一家公司工作。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ gēge zài Xīyǎtú de yì jiā gōngsī gōngzuò.
examples.english: My older brother works at a company in Seattle.

examples.hanzi: 西雅图的咖啡很有名。
examples.pinyin: Xīyǎtú de kāfēi hěn yǒumíng.
examples.english: Seattle's coffee is very famous.

components.note: 氵 (water) — harbours lie on water; also in 河 river, 海 sea.
巷 (xiàng) shares the rhyme -ang; only a loose sound clue.

example.hanzi: 这个港口每天有很多船进出。
example.pinyin: Zhège gǎngkǒu měitiān yǒu hěn duō chuán jìnchū.
example.english: Many ships come and go in this port every day.
example.fact: 港 is a harbor: 港口, 海港. 香港 (Hong Kong) means "fragrant harbor," and 港 alone is the short name for Hong Kong: 港币 (HK dollar), 港剧, 港人.

examples.hanzi: 他坐船去了香港。
examples.pinyin: Tā zuò chuán qù le Xiānggǎng.
examples.english: He took a boat to Hong Kong.

examples.hanzi: 渔船傍晚回到了港口。
examples.pinyin: Yúchuán bàngwǎn huídào le gǎngkǒu.
examples.english: The fishing boats returned to the harbor in the evening.

components.note: 来 (come) — it began as a picture of a wheat plant; the sound was borrowed for "come". 麦 (wheat) still shows it, with a root 夂 added.
一 (line) — dictionary reads 不 as a bird flying up toward the sky 一. The meaning 'not' is a borrowing, so the shape does not explain it today.
杯 (bēi) — a character that uses 不 as a loose sound clue (木 + 不). The sound is a hint only: 不 bù vs bēi.
及 (reach) — a hand 又 catching up with a person from behind: to reach, then and; seen in 以及, 及时.

example.hanzi: 快点,我们要来不及了!
example.pinyin: kuài diǎn, wǒmen yào láibují le!
example.english: Hurry up, we're going to be late!
example.fact: Japan's Shinkansen bullet trains have averaged an annual delay of less than one minute per train since the network opened in 1964, including time lost to earthquakes and typhoons — a level of precision that requires station staff to plan schedules down to fifteen-second increments.

examples.hanzi: 现在去机场已经来不及了。
examples.pinyin: Xiànzài qù jīchǎng yǐjīng lái bu jí le.
examples.english: It's too late to go to the airport now.

examples.hanzi: 作业太多了，我今晚写不完，明天来不及交。
examples.pinyin: Zuòyè tài duō le, wǒ jīnwǎn xiě bu wán, míngtiān lái bu jí jiāo.
examples.english: There's too much homework, and I can't finish tonight, so I won't have time to hand it in tomorrow.

components.note: 犭 (dog, animal) — animals, as in 狗, 猫, 猪: a wild animal.
王 (wáng) is a loose sound clue for kuáng; 王 also in 往 wǎng and 旺 wàng.
灬 (fire) — 灬 is fire at the bottom, as in 点, 照, 熟; 热 is heat.

example.hanzi: 球迷们对这场比赛表现出狂热的热情。
example.pinyin: qiúmímen duì zhè chǎng bǐsài biǎoxiàn chū kuángrè de rèqíng.
example.english: The fans showed fanatical enthusiasm for this match.
example.fact: During the Dutch 'tulip mania' of the 1630s, a single rare tulip bulb could sell for more than ten times the annual income of a skilled craftsman, with some bulbs reportedly trading for entire houses — one of the earliest documented speculative bubbles in economic history.

examples.hanzi: 他对摇滚乐有一种狂热的喜爱。
examples.pinyin: Tā duì yáogǔnyuè yǒu yì zhǒng kuángrè de xǐ'ài.
examples.english: He has a fanatical love for rock music.

examples.hanzi: 球迷们狂热地唱着队歌。
examples.pinyin: Qiúmímen kuángrè de chàngzhe duìgē.
examples.english: The fans sang the team song with fervor.

meanings: to provide financial or material support

components.note: 贝 (shell, old money) — marks money and gifts, as in 财, 货, 贵; 赞 is to help or praise, as with a gift.
力 (strength) — effort, as in 办, 男, 努; 助 is to lend strength.
且 (qiě) is a loose sound clue for zhù; 且 also sounds out 祖 zǔ, 租 zū and 姐 jiě.

example.hanzi: 这家公司赞助了奥运会代表队。
example.pinyin: zhè jiā gōngsī zànzhùle àoyùnhuì dàibiǎoduì.
example.english: This company sponsored the Olympic team.
example.fact: Coca-Cola has sponsored every Olympic Games since 1928, making it the longest continuously running corporate sponsorship in the history of sports.

examples.hanzi: 一家饮料公司赞助了这次比赛。
examples.pinyin: Yì jiā yǐnliào gōngsī zànzhù le zhè cì bǐsài.
examples.english: A drink company sponsored this competition.

examples.hanzi: 谢谢你们的赞助，活动才能顺利举行。
examples.pinyin: Xièxie nǐmen de zànzhù, huódòng cái néng shùnlì jǔxíng.
examples.english: Thank you for your sponsorship, which made the event possible.

components.note: 大 (big) — a front-facing person with arms and legs spread wide: big. As radical, 大 is in 天 sky, 太 too much, 夫 man.
人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.
牛 (ox) — cattle words like 牧 herd and 特 special; 物 first referred to livestock, then to things in general.
勿 (wù) sounds exactly like 物 — handy for recalling the pronunciation.

example.hanzi: 那位老人其实是政界的大人物。
example.pinyin: nà wèi lǎorén qíshí shì zhèngjiè de dàrénwù.
example.english: That old man is actually a big shot in politics.
example.fact: British anthropologist Robin Dunbar proposed in the 1990s that the human brain can maintain only about 150 meaningful social relationships at once, a limit he linked to the size of the neocortex — which may help explain why a handful of 'important people' loom disproportionately large within any one person's social world.

examples.hanzi: 他在公司里是个大人物。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài gōngsī lǐ shì ge dàrénwù.
examples.english: He is a big shot in the company.

examples.hanzi: 今天有几位大人物来参加开幕式。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān yǒu jǐ wèi dàrénwù lái cānjiā kāimùshì.
examples.english: Several VIPs came to the opening ceremony today.

components.note: 土 (earth) — a lump of earth on the ground; as a radical it marks land and soil, as in 地, 城, 块, 墙.
豆 — an old stemmed serving dish, later borrowed for beans; in 豆腐 tofu, 土豆 potato.

example.hanzi: 妈妈用土豆做了一道好吃的菜。
example.pinyin: māma yòng tǔdòu zuòle yī dào hǎochī de cài.
example.english: Mom made a delicious dish with potatoes.
example.fact: The potato was first domesticated more than 7,000 years ago by indigenous peoples near Lake Titicaca in the Andes, and Peru alone still cultivates over 4,000 distinct varieties today, ranging in color from white to deep purple.

examples.hanzi: 土豆炖牛肉是我最爱吃的菜。
examples.pinyin: Tǔdòu dùn niúròu shì wǒ zuì ài chī de cài.
examples.english: Beef stewed with potatoes is my favorite dish.

examples.hanzi: 我想买两斤土豆回家做薯条。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng mǎi liǎng jīn tǔdòu huíjiā zuò shǔtiáo.
examples.english: I want to buy two jin of potatoes to make fries at home.

components.note: 斤 (axe) — chopping, as in 所, 斩: freshly cut wood is new (薪 xīn is firewood).
亲 (qīn) is a close sound clue for xīn.
氵 (water) — marshy, watery land; also in 湖 lake, 河 river. 择 zé shares the right-hand part and the sound.
西 (west) — traditionally a bird settling on its nest at sunset, hence west; 西 turns up in 要 and 栖.

example.hanzi: 他去新泽西读大学。
example.pinyin: tā qù xīnzéxī dú dàxué.
example.english: He went to New Jersey for college.
example.fact: Despite its small size, New Jersey has the highest population density of any U.S. state and is also home to more diners per square mile than anywhere else in the country, a legacy of the state's role as a 20th-century manufacturing and rail hub.

examples.hanzi: 新泽西离纽约很近。
examples.pinyin: Xīnzéxī lí Niǔyuē hěn jìn.
examples.english: New Jersey is very close to New York.

examples.hanzi: 她在新泽西住了五年。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài Xīnzéxī zhù le wǔ nián.
examples.english: She lived in New Jersey for five years.

components.note: 彳 (step, conduct) — 彳 is a step or going, as in 行 and 往; 德 is conduct.
心 (heart) — 心 is the heart — the old 悳 was a straight 直 heart, so upright inner conduct.
兄 (older brother) — the bottom part. Dictionary story: a weapon 十 used to subdue a beast 兄. A memory aid; the origin is debated. In names (杰克, 麦克) 克 is only sound.
十 (ten) — the top bar. Memory aid: ten times stronger than your brother 兄 — to overcome, as in 克服.
艹 (grass, plants) — the plant radical, as in 花 flower, 草 grass. In 萨 it no longer carries meaning; 萨 only appears in transliterations such as 菩萨 bodhisattva.
产 (to produce) — the lower right part. Memory aid: sound-only character; learn it as a unit from 菩萨, 萨克斯.
斤 (axe) — the original idea was chopping with an axe, as in 新, 斩 chop, 断 break; today 斯 is mostly a sound-borrowing syllable sī in foreign names like 俄罗斯.

example.hanzi: 德克萨斯是美国面积最大的州之一。
example.pinyin: dékèsàsī shì měiguó miànjī zuìdà de zhōu zhī yī.
example.english: Texas is one of the largest states in the US by area.
example.fact: Texas was an independent republic for nearly a decade (1836-1845) before joining the United States, and it even had its own navy and its own currency, called Texas dollars, before annexation folded it into the Union as the 28th state.

examples.hanzi: 德克萨斯的夏天非常热。
examples.pinyin: Dékèsàsī de xiàtiān fēicháng rè.
examples.english: Summers in Texas are very hot.

examples.hanzi: 他的叔叔在德克萨斯开牧场。
examples.pinyin: Tā de shūshu zài Dékèsàsī kāi mùchǎng.
examples.english: His uncle runs a ranch in Texas.

components.note: 衣 (clothing) — cloth ripping apart; also as 衤 in 衬, 被.
列 (liè) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 烈 liè.
纟 (silk, simplified 糸) — sewing with thread; also in 红 red, 级 level.
逢 (féng) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 蓬 péng and 篷 péng.

example.hanzi: 墙上出现了一条裂缝。
example.pinyin: qiáng shàng chūxiànle yī tiáo lièfèng.
example.english: A crack appeared on the wall.
example.fact: Kintsugi, a centuries-old Japanese art form, repairs cracks in broken pottery with gold-dusted lacquer rather than hiding them, treating the fracture as part of the object's history instead of a flaw to conceal.

examples.hanzi: 地震后，路面上有很多裂缝。
examples.pinyin: Dìzhèn hòu, lùmiàn shàng yǒu hěn duō lièfèng.
examples.english: After the earthquake, there were many cracks in the road.

examples.hanzi: 阳光从云层的裂缝里照下来。
examples.pinyin: Yángguāng cóng yúncéng de lièfèng lǐ zhào xiàlái.
examples.english: Sunlight shone down through a gap in the clouds.

components.note: 工 (work) — a carpenter's tool shape: work, craftsman. 工 is a sound series: 红 hóng, 江 jiāng, 功 gōng, 空 kōng.
禾 (grain) — grain radical — 程 first meant to measure grain, hence standard, then course and journey; also in 种, 秋, 稿.
呈 (chéng) — same sound — 程 is chéng; 呈 also sounds out 逞 chěng.

example.hanzi: 他大学学的是土木工程。
example.pinyin: tā dàxué xué de shì tǔmù gōngchéng.
example.english: He studied civil engineering in college.
example.fact: The Roman Pantheon, completed around 128 AD, still holds the record for the world's largest unreinforced concrete dome — a feat of engineering that relied on a concrete mixture graded lighter toward the top, using volcanic pumice instead of heavier aggregate.

examples.hanzi: 这项工程预计明年完成。
examples.pinyin: Zhè xiàng gōngchéng yùjì míngnián wánchéng.
examples.english: This project is expected to be completed next year.

examples.hanzi: 他是一名桥梁工程师，参加过很多大工程。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì yì míng qiáoliáng gōngchéngshī, cānjiā guo hěn duō dà gōngchéng.
examples.english: He is a bridge engineer and has taken part in many big projects.

components.note: 亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 位; 偶 first meant a figure or doll, then a pair.
禺 (yú) is a loose sound clue; same part in 遇 yù, 愚 yú, 寓 yù.
灬 (fire) — heat and burning, as in 热 hot, 点 dot, 照 shine. 然 first meant "to burn" (燃 rán adds 火 later); "so, naturally" is borrowed.
肰 (rán) gives the exact sound and shows up in 燃 rán.

example.hanzi: 我们的相遇纯属偶然。
example.pinyin: wǒmen de xiāngyù chúnshǔ ǒurán.
example.english: Our meeting was purely by chance.
example.fact: Alexander Fleming discovered penicillin in 1928 purely by accident, after noticing that mold had contaminated a petri dish he'd left uncovered and was killing the bacteria growing around it — a chance observation that launched the age of antibiotics.

examples.hanzi: 我偶然在街上遇见了老同学。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ ǒurán zài jiē shàng yùjiàn le lǎo tóngxué.
examples.english: I ran into an old classmate on the street by chance.

examples.hanzi: 这不是偶然，而是努力的结果。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bú shì ǒurán, ér shì nǔlì de jiéguǒ.
examples.english: This isn't chance, but the result of hard work.

components.note: 火 (fire) — heat and burning, as in 灯 lamp, 烧 burn, 热 hot: a hot, fevered head, hence vexed.
页 (head) is a loose sound clue for fán; as a meaning part 页 means head or page.
人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.

example.hanzi: 邻居家的狗整晚叫,真烦人。
example.pinyin: línjū jiā de gǒu zhěngwǎn jiào, zhēn fánrén.
example.english: The neighbor's dog barked all night, so annoying.
example.fact: Mosquitoes' high-pitched whine is the sound of their wings beating up to 800 times per second, and only female mosquitoes bite — they need the protein in blood to develop their eggs, while males feed solely on nectar.

examples.hanzi: 别烦人了，我在做作业。
examples.pinyin: Bié fánrén le, wǒ zài zuò zuòyè.
examples.english: Stop being annoying, I'm doing homework.

examples.hanzi: 下雨天出门真烦人。
examples.pinyin: Xiàyǔ tiān chūmén zhēn fánrén.
examples.english: Going out on rainy days is so annoying.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — 讠 is the simplified 言 (speech), as in 说, 话, 读; 讲 is to talk and explain.
井 (jǐng) — near sound — 讲 is jiǎng; the old form had a different right side, so this is only a loose hint.
讠 (speech) — 讠 is the simplified 言 (speech), as in 说, 话, 读; 讲 is to talk and explain.
井 (jǐng) — near sound — 讲 is jiǎng; the old form had a different right side, so this is only a loose hint.

example.hanzi: 你给我们讲讲这次旅行的故事吧。
example.pinyin: nǐ gěi wǒmen jiǎngjiǎng zhè cì lǔxíng de gùshì ba.
example.english: Tell us a bit about the story of this trip.
example.fact: Oral storytelling predates writing by tens of thousands of years, and some Aboriginal Australian oral traditions have been shown by geologists to accurately describe coastline changes from sea-level rise that occurred more than 7,000 years ago, passed down across roughly 300 generations.

examples.hanzi: 请你给大家讲讲这本书的内容。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng nǐ gěi dàjiā jiǎngjiang zhè běn shū de nèiróng.
examples.english: Please tell everyone a bit about the content of this book.

examples.hanzi: 老师，您能再讲讲这个词的用法吗？
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī, nín néng zài jiǎngjiang zhège cí de yòngfǎ ma?
examples.english: Teacher, could you explain how to use this word once more?

components.note: 广 (house) — the top-left cover, as in 店 shop and 床 bed; it marks a building or room.
隶 (servant) — inside 广. Dictionary story: a home with a servant, healthy and untroubled, hence 健康 health; origin is uncertain, so memory aid only.

example.hanzi: 祝你身体健康。
example.pinyin: Zhù nǐ shēntǐ jiànkāng.
example.english: I wish you good health.
example.fact: 康 on its own is formal. It builds 健康 (health), 康复 (to recover), and 小康 ("moderately well-off"), a policy phrase for a comfortable society. 康熙 is the famed Kangxi emperor.

examples.hanzi: 医生说我的身体很健康。
examples.pinyin: Yīshēng shuō wǒ de shēntǐ hěn jiànkāng.
examples.english: The doctor said my body is very healthy.

examples.hanzi: 祝您新年平安，健康幸福。
examples.pinyin: Zhù nín xīnnián píng'ān, jiànkāng xìngfú.
examples.english: Wishing you a peaceful, healthy and happy new year.

components.note: 舛 (two opposed feet) — the dancer's footwork; 無 (wú) above is a loose sound clue, as it once meant dance itself.
亻 (person) — person radical — 伴 is a companion, as in 伙伴.
半 (bàn) — same sound — 伴 is bàn, like 半; 半 also sounds out 拌 bàn and 叛 pàn.

example.hanzi: 她在舞会上找到了一个好舞伴。
example.pinyin: tā zài wǔhuì shàng zhǎodàole yī gè hǎo wǔbàn.
example.english: She found a good dance partner at the dance party.
example.fact: The tango originated in the working-class port neighborhoods of Buenos Aires and Montevideo in the late 19th century, blending African, European, and South American musical traditions, and was considered so scandalous at first that some ballrooms banned it outright.

examples.hanzi: 他是我跳舞时的舞伴。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì wǒ tiàowǔ shí de wǔbàn.
examples.english: He is my partner when I dance.

examples.hanzi: 舞会开始前，我还没找到舞伴。
examples.pinyin: Wǔhuì kāishǐ qián, wǒ hái méi zhǎodào wǔbàn.
examples.english: I hadn't found a dance partner before the ball began.

components.note: 止 (foot) — a foot heading straight for a target line: upright, correct. 正 gives sound to 证 zhèng, 整 zhěng and 政 zhèng.
當 (traditional) — 田 field under 尚 (shàng), 尚 being a loose sound hint for dāng. 当 keeps only a squashed top and a few strokes of it.
尚 (shàng) — the top part of 當; only a loose sound clue today. 当 is dāng (to act as, should) or dàng (appropriate).

example.hanzi: 他正当我们需要帮助的时候出现了。
example.pinyin: tā zhèngdāng wǒmen xūyào bāngzhù de shíhòu chūxiànle.
example.english: He appeared just when we needed help.
example.fact: Arctic terns time their migration so precisely that they arrive at breeding grounds just as the local insect population peaks, completing a round trip of roughly 70,000 kilometers each year — the longest annual migration of any animal on Earth.

examples.hanzi: 正当我要出门时，电话响了。
examples.pinyin: Zhèngdāng wǒ yào chūmén shí, diànhuà xiǎng le.
examples.english: Just as I was about to go out, the phone rang.

examples.hanzi: 正当壮年的他，每天都精力充沛。
examples.pinyin: Zhèngdāng zhuàngnián de tā, měi tiān dōu jīnglì chōngpèi.
examples.english: In the prime of life, he is full of energy every day.

components.note: 土 (earth) — falling to the ground; also in 地 ground, 城 city.
艹 (grass, plants) — plants and leaves: 花, 草, 叶; 落 is leaves falling.
洛 (luò) sounds exactly like 落; related to 各 gè in 路 lù.

example.hanzi: 他因为赌博而逐渐堕落。
example.pinyin: tā yīnwèi dǔbó ér zhújiàn duòluò.
example.english: He gradually degenerated because of gambling.
example.fact: Roman emperors of the 3rd century AD progressively debased the denarius, the empire's standard silver coin, from nearly pure silver to barely 5% silver content within decades — a slow monetary collapse that historians link to the runaway inflation and instability of the empire's darkest years.

examples.hanzi: 不良的生活习惯会让人慢慢堕落。
examples.pinyin: Bùliáng de shēnghuó xíguàn huì ràng rén mànmàn duòluò.
examples.english: Bad habits can slowly make a person degenerate.

examples.hanzi: 他不想让自己堕落下去。
examples.pinyin: Tā bù xiǎng ràng zìjǐ duòluò xiàqù.
examples.english: He doesn't want to let himself sink further.

components.note: 羽 (feather) — wings and flight, as in 翼 wing, 习, 翻 flip.
支 (zhī) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 枝 zhī and 肢 zhī.
⺼ (flesh, 肉月旁) — body-part radical, as in 脸, 腿; 膀 is the upper arm or shoulder.
旁 (páng) is a loose hint for bǎng; 榜 bǎng and 磅 bàng share it.

example.hanzi: 那只鸟张开翅膀飞走了。
example.pinyin: nà zhī niǎo zhāngkāi chìbǎng fēizǒule.
example.english: That bird spread its wings and flew away.
example.fact: The wandering albatross has the largest wingspan of any living bird, up to 3.5 meters, which lets it glide for hours over the open ocean on rising air currents without flapping — some individuals have been tracked flying over 10,000 kilometers in a single foraging trip.

examples.hanzi: 小鸟的翅膀受伤了。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎo niǎo de chìbǎng shòushāng le.
examples.english: The little bird's wing is injured.

examples.hanzi: 天使有一对白色的翅膀。
examples.pinyin: Tiānshǐ yǒu yí duì báisè de chìbǎng.
examples.english: Angels have a pair of white wings.

components.note: 丹 (cinnabar) — an ancient picture of a mine with cinnabar in it; 丹 is red, as in 牡丹.
尼 (ní) — 尼 sounds out 泥 ní and 呢 ní; here it appears mostly in foreign names such as 丹尼.
⺈ (bent figure) — the top part of 尔, a variant stroke group. 尔 is an old form of 'you'; today it appears mainly in foreign names like 比尔 Bill.
小 (small) — the bottom part and radical, as in 少 few. The shape does not explain 'you'; the character is now mostly sound-borrowed.

example.hanzi: 丹尼尔昨天搬到了这个城市。
example.pinyin: dānní'ěr zuótiān bāndàole zhège chéngshì.
example.english: Daniel moved to this city yesterday.
example.fact: The biblical figure Daniel is said to have survived a night in a den of lions unharmed; historically, lions were once common across the Middle East and Southern Europe, and the last wild Asiatic lion within that historic range wasn't wiped out until the early 20th century.

examples.hanzi: 丹尼尔是我弟弟的同学。
examples.pinyin: Dānní'ěr shì wǒ dìdi de tóngxué.
examples.english: Daniel is my younger brother's classmate.

examples.hanzi: 你把这个包裹交给丹尼尔吧。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ bǎ zhège bāoguǒ jiāo gěi Dānní'ěr ba.
examples.english: Please hand this parcel to Daniel.

components.note: 手 (hand) — 手 as in 拿, 打, 拳; 掌 is the palm of the hand, then to control.
尚 (shàng) — near sound — 掌 is zhǎng; 尚 also sounds out 常 cháng, 堂 táng and 赏 shǎng.
聲 (traditional) — a hanging stone chime struck, with 耳 (ear) below: a sound you hear. 声 keeps only the top, so the picture is mostly lost.
士 (scholar) — the top of 声 is only a leftover of the old chime, not 'scholar'. Do not read meaning into it.

example.hanzi: 演讲结束后,现场爆发出热烈的掌声。
example.pinyin: yǎnjiǎng jiéshù hòu, xiànchǎng bàofā chū rèliè de zhǎngshēng.
example.english: After the speech ended, the audience burst into warm applause.
example.fact: Physicists studying applause have found that when an audience claps enthusiastically, individual clappers unconsciously synchronize their rhythm for a few seconds, then deliberately break apart into randomness again because irregular clapping actually sounds louder overall — a pattern first documented in a study of Eastern European theater crowds.

examples.hanzi: 听到精彩的表演，观众响起了掌声。
examples.pinyin: Tīngdào jīngcǎi de biǎoyǎn, guānzhòng xiǎngqǐ le zhǎngshēng.
examples.english: After the wonderful performance, the audience broke into applause.

examples.hanzi: 让我们用掌声欢迎新同学！
examples.pinyin: Ràng wǒmen yòng zhǎngshēng huānyíng xīn tóngxué!
examples.english: Let's welcome the new classmate with applause!

components.note: 木 (tree) — 杰 is simplified from 傑; a tall tree makes a handy picture for an outstanding person standing tall.
王 (jade, 斜玉旁) — precious jade, an omen of luck; also in 球 ball, 珠 pearl.
耑 (duān) is a loose clue; it also sounds out 端 duān.

example.hanzi: 杰瑞养了一只可爱的猫。
example.pinyin: jiéruì yǎngle yī zhī kě'ài de māo.
example.english: Jerry has a cute cat.
example.fact: The cartoon mouse Jerry, star of the classic 'Tom and Jerry' shorts, was almost named 'Jinx' before animators settled on Jerry — the series went on to win seven Academy Awards for Best Animated Short Film, tying it with Looney Tunes for the most in that category.

examples.hanzi: 杰瑞住在我们的隔壁。
examples.pinyin: Jiéruì zhù zài wǒmen de gébì.
examples.english: Jerry lives next door to us.

examples.hanzi: 杰瑞今天要去机场接朋友。
examples.pinyin: Jiéruì jīntiān yào qù jīchǎng jiē péngyou.
examples.english: Jerry is going to the airport today to pick up a friend.

components.note: 纟 (silk thread, simplified 糸) — threads and ties, as in 红, 给, 经; 结 is a knot.
吉 (jí) is a close sound clue for jié; 吉 also sounds out 洁 jié.
尸 (body) — a body with 毛 fur behind it is a tail; 尸 also in 屁, 尿 and 层.
毛 (hair, fur) — the furry tip hanging off the back.

example.hanzi: 这部电影的结尾让人意外。
example.pinyin: zhè bù diànyǐng de jiéwěi ràng rén yìwài.
example.english: The ending of this movie is surprising.
example.fact: In music, a 'coda' — from the Italian word for 'tail' — is a passage that brings a piece to a formal close after its main themes have finished; Beethoven was especially known for writing unusually long codas, sometimes nearly as long as a movement's main body, to give his symphonies a more dramatic conclusion.

examples.hanzi: 这篇文章的结尾写得很精彩。
examples.pinyin: Zhè piān wénzhāng de jiéwěi xiě de hěn jīngcǎi.
examples.english: The ending of this article is very well written.

examples.hanzi: 会议在大家的掌声中结尾。
examples.pinyin: Huìyì zài dàjiā de zhǎngshēng zhōng jiéwěi.
examples.english: The meeting wound up amid everyone's applause.

components.note: 月 (flesh/meat, not moon here) — oldest form is a hand holding a piece of meat, "to possess"; 月 as meat also appears in 肉 words like 肚 belly and 脑 brain.
口 (mouth) — calling out; 夕 (evening) beside it: in the dark you cannot be seen, so you call your name.

example.hanzi: 这家餐厅因为牛肉面而有名。
example.pinyin: zhè jiā cāntīng yīnwèi niúròumiàn ér yǒumíng.
example.english: This restaurant is famous for its beef noodle soup.
example.fact: In 1968, artist Andy Warhol predicted that 'in the future, everyone will be famous for 15 minutes' — a line written for an exhibition catalogue that, decades before social media, anticipated how easily ordinary people could achieve brief viral fame.

examples.hanzi: 这位老师在我们学校很有名。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi lǎoshī zài wǒmen xuéxiào hěn yǒumíng.
examples.english: This teacher is very well known at our school.

examples.hanzi: 这座山以日出有名。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò shān yǐ rìchū yǒumíng.
examples.english: This mountain is famous for its sunrises.

components.note: 页 (head, page) — marks the head and face, as in 顶, 题, 顺; 预 is thinking ahead.
予 (yǔ) hints at the sound: 预 yù is close, as in 豫 yù.
斗 (dipper, measure) — measuring grain and liquids: 科, 斜, 升; 料 is rice 米 measured out, then material.

example.hanzi: 事情的发展完全出乎我们的预料。
example.pinyin: shìqíng de fāzhǎn wánquán chūhū wǒmen de yùliào.
example.english: The development of the matter was completely beyond our expectations.
example.fact: Modern five-day weather forecasts are now roughly as accurate as one-day forecasts were in the 1980s, an improvement driven by satellite data, supercomputers, and better mathematical models of the atmosphere.

examples.hanzi: 比赛的结果在我们的预料之中。
examples.pinyin: Bǐsài de jiéguǒ zài wǒmen de yùliào zhī zhōng.
examples.english: The result of the match was within our expectations.

examples.hanzi: 谁也没有预料到会下这么大的雨。
examples.pinyin: Shéi yě méiyǒu yùliào dào huì xià zhème dà de yǔ.
examples.english: No one expected such heavy rain.

components.note: 讠 (speech; traditional 言) — marks speaking and language, as in 说 say, 话 speech, 请 request; 谜 is a riddle, words that puzzle.
迷 (mí) — same sound: 谜 mí. 迷 means lost, confused.

example.hanzi: 这个谜语太难了，我猜不出来。
example.pinyin: Zhège míyǔ tài nán le, wǒ cāi bu chū lái.
example.english: This riddle is too hard, so I cannot guess it.
example.fact: 谜 is a riddle or mystery: 谜语, 谜团 (puzzle), 千古之谜 (an age-old mystery). Guessing lantern riddles (猜灯谜) is a traditional Lantern Festival activity. A Beijing form 谜儿 reads mèir.

examples.hanzi: 他给我们出了一个谜语。
examples.pinyin: Tā gěi wǒmen chū le yí ge míyǔ.
examples.english: He gave us a riddle.

examples.hanzi: 这件事到现在还是一个谜。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì dào xiànzài háishi yí ge mí.
examples.english: This matter is still a mystery to this day.

components.note: 高 (tall) — a drawing of a tall tower building. 高 also sounds out 糕 gāo (cake), 搞 gǎo and 稿 gǎo.
辶 (movement, road) — 辶 marks going and moving — 速 is speed, as in 快速 and 速度.
束 (shù) — near sound — 速 is sù, same syllable with different initial.

example.hanzi: 我们开车走高速去了那个城市。
example.pinyin: wǒmen kāichē zǒu gāosù qùle nàge chéngshì.
example.english: We drove on the expressway to that city.
example.fact: NASA's Parker Solar Probe is the fastest human-made object ever built, reaching speeds of over 690,000 kilometers per hour as it dives close to the Sun — fast enough to travel from New York to Los Angeles in about 21 seconds.

examples.hanzi: 高速上的车很多，我们开得很慢。
examples.pinyin: Gāosù shàng de chē hěn duō, wǒmen kāi de hěn màn.
examples.english: There are many cars on the highway, so we drove slowly.

examples.hanzi: 这列火车是高速的，只要两小时。
examples.pinyin: Zhè liè huǒchē shì gāosù de, zhǐyào liǎng xiǎoshí.
examples.english: This train is high-speed and takes only two hours.

meanings: variant of 贊同|赞同[zan4 tong2]

components.note: 贝 (shell, old money) — marks money and gifts, as in 财, 货, 贵; 赞 is to help or praise, as with a gift.
口 (mouth) — speech, as in 吃, 唱, 问: voices in unison. 同 also gives sound to 铜 tóng, 桶 tǒng, 洞 dòng.

example.hanzi: 大多数股东都赞同这项计划。
example.pinyin: dà duōshù gǔdōng dōu zàntóng zhè xiàng jìhuà.
example.english: Most shareholders agree with this plan.
example.fact: Switzerland holds more national referendums than any other country, with citizens voting on dozens of proposals covering everything from immigration policy to tunnel construction — a direct-democracy tradition dating back to the 19th century.

examples.hanzi: 我完全赞同你的意见。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ wánquán zàntóng nǐ de yìjiàn.
examples.english: I completely agree with your opinion.

examples.hanzi: 老师赞同我们去郊游。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī zàntóng wǒmen qù jiāoyóu.
examples.english: The teacher approves of us going on the outing.

meanings: variant of 合併|合并[he2 bing4]

components.note: 合 (join) — a lid fitting over an opening 口: things that fit together. 合 also appears in 答 dá, 给 gěi and 拾 shí.
并 (combine) — simplified from 並, which showed two figures standing side by side; hence together, also, and (并且).

example.hanzi: 两家公司决定合并成一家。
example.pinyin: liǎng jiā gōngsī juédìng hébìng chéng yī jiā.
example.english: The two companies decided to merge into one.
example.fact: At Manaus, Brazil, the dark waters of the Rio Negro and the pale, sediment-rich Amazon River merge but do not fully mix for several kilometers downstream, flowing side by side in a visible line known as the 'meeting of waters' due to differences in temperature, speed, and density.

examples.hanzi: 请把这两个文件合并成一个。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ zhè liǎng ge wénjiàn hébìng chéng yí ge.
examples.english: Please merge these two files into one.

examples.hanzi: 两个班合并以后，一共有六十个学生。
examples.pinyin: Liǎng ge bān hébìng yǐhòu, yígòng yǒu liùshí ge xuésheng.
examples.english: After the two classes were merged, there were sixty students in all.

meanings: stylized gait used by performers on stage

components.note: 台 (tái) as a sound part appears in 抬 tái, 胎 tāi, 苔 tái, and also in 治 zhì and 始 shǐ.
止 (foot) — two footprints, one above the other, make a step; the same 止 is in 走 walk and 跑 run.

example.hanzi: 演员在台上走台步显得格外优雅。
example.pinyin: yǎnyuán zài tái shàng zǒu táibù xiǎnde géwài yōuyǎ.
example.english: The actor's stage walk appeared especially graceful.
example.fact: Peking opera, formalized in the late 18th century, trains performers for years in stylized walks, gestures, and acrobatics before they ever take a lead role — a single sleeve toss or turn can take months of repetitive drilling to master.

examples.hanzi: 京剧演员的台步很讲究。
examples.pinyin: Jīngjù yǎnyuán de táibù hěn jiǎngjiu.
examples.english: Peking opera performers pay great attention to their stage walk.

examples.hanzi: 她练了很久才学会这种台步。
examples.pinyin: Tā liàn le hěn jiǔ cái xuéhuì zhè zhǒng táibù.
examples.english: She practiced for a long time before learning this stage walk.

components.note: 上 (above) — a mark above a line, the mirror of 下 below.
氵 (water) — water and flow, as in 河, 海, 清: 演 first meant a long flowing stream, then spreading out and performing.
寅 (yín) is a close sound clue for yǎn.

example.hanzi: 这部话剧下周将在剧院上演。
example.pinyin: zhè bù huàjù xià zhōu jiāng zài jùyuàn shàngyǎn.
example.english: This play will be staged at the theater next week.
example.fact: Shakespeare's Globe Theatre, built in London in 1599, could hold around 3,000 spectators standing and seated around an open-air stage; after burning down in 1613 when a cannon effect during a performance of Henry VIII set the thatched roof alight, it was rebuilt within a year.

examples.hanzi: 这部电影下个月在全国上演。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng xià ge yuè zài quánguó shàngyǎn.
examples.english: This movie will be shown nationwide next month.

examples.hanzi: 学校的话剧今晚上演。
examples.pinyin: Xuéxiào de huàjù jīnwǎn shàngyǎn.
examples.english: The school play is being staged tonight.

components.note: 史 (history) — a hand 又 holding a record, the scribe. 史 sounds the same as 使 shǐ and 驶 shǐ.
艹 (plants) — marks plants, as in 花, 草, 茶; 蒂 is the stem of a fruit or flower.
帝 (dì) gives the sound exactly: 蒂 dì, also in 啼 tí and 缔 dì.
大 (person) — a man with a hairpin 一 on his head, a grown man; 夫 also gives 扶 fú and 肤 fū.

example.hanzi: 史蒂夫是我们公司的技术总监。
example.pinyin: shǐdìfū shì wǒmen gōngsī de jìshù zǒngjiān.
example.english: Steve is our company's technical director.
example.fact: Steve Jobs co-founded Apple in his parents' garage in Los Altos, California in 1976, and that same garage was later designated a historic site by the city, even though the company quickly outgrew it and moved to larger offices within a couple of years.

examples.hanzi: 史蒂夫每天骑车上班。
examples.pinyin: Shǐdìfū měi tiān qí chē shàngbān.
examples.english: Steve cycles to work every day.

examples.hanzi: 我昨天遇见了史蒂夫。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuótiān yùjiàn le Shǐdìfū.
examples.english: I ran into Steve yesterday.

components.note: 用 (use) — early picture is debated: a pail, a fenced enclosure or a hung bell. Memory aid: a door-frame 冂 with a cross-bar — a tool 'put to use' (使用, 不用).
于 (yú) is a sound clue for 宇 yǔ and 芋 yù; it is a light grammar word meaning "at, to".

example.hanzi: 这种材料主要用于建筑行业。
example.pinyin: zhè zhǒng cáiliào zhǔyào yòngyú jiànzhù hángyè.
example.english: This material is mainly used in the construction industry.
example.fact: Graphene, a single layer of carbon atoms arranged in a hexagonal lattice, is roughly 200 times stronger than steel by weight and is being explored for use in everything from flexible electronics to water filtration membranes since its isolation was first demonstrated in 2004.

examples.hanzi: 这笔钱只能用于买书。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bǐ qián zhǐ néng yòngyú mǎi shū.
examples.english: This money can only be used for buying books.

examples.hanzi: 这种药不能用于儿童。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng yào bù néng yòngyú értóng.
examples.english: This medicine cannot be used on children.

components.note: 将 (jiāng) is the trimmed top part: 奖 jiǎng sounds like 桨 jiǎng and 浆 jiāng.
子 (child) — a child learning under a roof: the top shows hands over a house, and the child 子 below. Also gives 觉 jué its upper part.
今 (jīn) — the top part hints the sound — 金 is jīn, like 今; 金 means gold and metal.
金 (metal) — as a radical it shrinks to 钅 in simplified characters — 钱 money, 铁 iron, 钟 clock, 银 silver.

example.hanzi: 她凭优异的成绩获得了全额奖学金。
example.pinyin: tā píng yōuyì de chéngjì huòdéle quán'é jiǎngxuéjīn.
example.english: She earned a full scholarship with her excellent grades.
example.fact: The Rhodes Scholarship, one of the oldest and most prestigious international graduate scholarships, was established in 1902 through the will of British businessman Cecil Rhodes and funds recipients from dozens of countries to study at the University of Oxford.

examples.hanzi: 我申请了一笔奖学金。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ shēnqǐng le yì bǐ jiǎngxuéjīn.
examples.english: I applied for a scholarship.

examples.hanzi: 他靠奖学金读完了大学。
examples.pinyin: Tā kào jiǎngxuéjīn dúwán le dàxué.
examples.english: He finished university on a scholarship.
